newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine, Belarus freak storm victims rise to 12.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine, Belarus freak storm victims rise to 12.

text.p: Twelve people were killed in Ukraine and Belarus in a fierce summer storm that felled trees, ripped off roofs and tore down power lines, officials in the two former Soviet republics said on Tuesday.

"Latest information shows one more death, bringing the total to nine. The number of injured has risen to 46 from 32 people, and 27 of those are in hospital," Natalya Tsushko of the Ukraine Emergencies Ministry press service told Reuters.
The storm wove a path of destruction north to neighbouring Belarus, where a civil defence spokesman said three people were killed near the capital, Minsk.
In Ukraine, some 850 towns and villages were left without electricity and hundreds of coal miners were rescued after spending the night underground because of power cuts.
Some people were killed after hiding under trees which then fell on them, while others were electrocuted by power lines, Tsushko said.
Teams were checking damage to spring crops, officials said.
In neighbouring Romania12 people were killed last week in flash floods which followed heavy rains and hail.
The storms also damaged seasonal crops, mainly wheat and maize, on almost 100,000 hectares (250,000 acres). The Agriculture Ministry put losses at 200 billion lei ($28 million).
